books.name: My Cat Coco
books.focus: a · an · is · has · on · her

items.tip: Use a before one thing that starts with a consonant sound: a cat, a little cat.

no.an: an goes before a vowel sound (an apple), but little starts with l.
no.is: is is a 'be' word; before little cat we need a.
no.on: on tells where something is; it can't go before little cat here.

items.say: I have a little cat.
items.ask: I have blank little cat.

items.tip: One thing (her name) → is. I am, you are, he/she/it is.

no.are: are is for you, we, they or more than one; her name is one thing.
no.am: am only goes with I: I am.
no.has: has means owning something; a name can't own Coco!

items.say: Her name is Coco.
items.ask: Her name blank Coco.

items.s: She ___ white paws and a pink nose.
items.tip: he/she/it has; I/you/we/they have. Coco is one cat, so she has.

no.have: have is for I, you, we and they; she needs has.
no.is: She is white paws? No! Paws are something she has.
no.are: are is for more than one; Coco is one cat.

items.say: She has white paws and a pink nose.
items.ask: She blank white paws and a pink nose.

items.s: Coco likes to sleep ___ my bed.
items.tip: on my bed = on top of it (in my bed = under the covers: also right!).

no.at: at is for a place or a time (at school, at seven); we sleep on or in a bed.
no.of: of shows belonging (a cup of milk); it doesn't tell where.
no.to: to shows moving towards a place (go to school).

items.say: Coco likes to sleep on my bed.
items.ask: Coco likes to sleep blank my bed.

items.tip: and joins two things she does: eats fish and drinks milk.

no.is: eats fish is drinks milk? We need a joining word: and.
no.a: a goes before one thing (a cat), not before drinks.
no.at: at tells a place or time; to join two actions we need and.

items.say: She eats fish and drinks milk.
items.ask: She eats fish blank drinks milk.

items.s: Every morning, she plays with ___ orange ball.
items.tip: Use an before a vowel sound: an orange, an apple, an egg.

no.a: orange starts with a vowel sound, so it's an, not a.
no.on: on tells where; before orange ball we need an.
no.is: is is a 'be' word; it can't go before orange ball here.

items.say: Every morning, she plays with an orange ball.
items.ask: Every morning, she plays with blank orange ball.

items.tip: can + verb = she is able to do it. No -s after can: she can jump.

no.cans: can never takes -s: she can jump.
no.is: is jump isn't English; is goes with -ing: is jumping.
no.has: has jump isn't English; has goes with a thing: has a ball.

items.say: Coco can jump very high!
items.ask: Coco blank jump very high!

items.tip: After a doing word we say her, not she: I love her. (him for a boy cat!)

no.she: she comes before a doing word (She runs); after love we say her.
no.he: he comes before a doing word, and Coco is a girl cat: her.
no.is: I love is? We need who we love: her.

items.say: I love her very much.
items.ask: I love blank very much.

items.s: There ___ lots of flowers in the park.
items.tip: There are + more than one thing (lots of flowers). There is + one thing.

no.is: is is for one thing; lots of flowers are many, so are.
no.be: be needs a helper (will be, can be); here we need are.

items.say: There are lots of flowers in the park.
items.ask: There blank lots of flowers in the park.

items.s: Two girls are playing ___ a red ball.
items.tip: We play with a ball, a toy or a friend.

no.on: playing on a ball means standing on it!
no.at: at is for a place or a time, not a toy.
no.of: of shows belonging; we play with a ball.

items.say: Two girls are playing with a red ball.
items.ask: Two girls are playing blank a red ball.

items.s: ___ are my sisters, Amy and Jo.
items.tip: They = more than one person, before the verb: They are my sisters.

no.Them: Them comes after a doing word (I see them), not at the start.
no.She: She is one girl, but Amy and Jo are two: They.
no.It: It is for one thing, not two people.

items.say: They are my sisters, Amy and Jo.
items.ask: Blank are my sisters, Amy and Jo.

items.s: My dad is sitting ___ a bench.
items.tip: We sit on a bench, a chair or the grass.

no.of: of shows belonging, not a place.
no.to: to shows moving towards a place, not sitting.
no.an: an goes before a vowel sound, and bench already has a.

items.say: My dad is sitting on a bench.
items.ask: My dad is sitting blank a bench.

items.tip: he/she/it is + -ing for now: He is reading.

no.are: are is for you, we and they; he needs is.
no.have: have is for I, you, we and they, and it doesn't go before -ing here.

items.say: He is reading a book.
items.ask: He blank reading a book.

items.tip: have got = have: We have got a basket. I've got a cat.

no.get: have get isn't English; have got means have.
no.gets: gets is for he, she or it, and have gets isn't English.
no.a: There's already a before picnic basket; two a's don't work.

items.say: We have got a picnic basket.
items.ask: We have blank a picnic basket.

items.tip: an before a vowel sound: an apple, an orange.

no.a: apple starts with a vowel sound, so we say an apple.
no.on: on tells where; before apple we need an.
no.is: is is a 'be' word; it can't go before apple here.

items.say: Mum gives me an apple.
items.ask: Mum gives me blank apple.

items.tip: I like / I love + a thing. No -s after I.

no.likes: likes is for he, she or it; with I we say like.
no.am: I am the park? You aren't a park!
no.is: is is for he, she or it; it doesn't go with I.

items.say: I like the park very much!
items.ask: I blank the park very much!

items.tip: a before one thing with a consonant sound: a small dog.

no.an: small starts with a consonant sound, so a, not an.
no.are: Ben is are isn't English; one 'be' word is enough.
no.on: on tells where; before small brown dog we need a.

items.say: Ben is a small brown dog.
items.ask: Ben is blank small brown dog.

items.tip: He = one boy or boy animal, before the verb: He lives…

no.His: His shows belonging (his ball); before lives we need He.
no.Him: Him comes after a doing word (I like him).
no.We: We is more than one, and we say We live, not We lives.

items.say: He lives with the Lee family.
items.ask: Blank lives with the Lee family.

items.tip: at + a clock time: at seven o'clock, at half past two.

no.in: in is for months and years (in May), not clock times.
no.on: on is for days (on Monday), not clock times.
no.of: of shows belonging, not a time.

items.say: Ben gets up at seven o'clock.
items.ask: Ben gets up blank seven o'clock.

items.s: He eats ___ breakfast in the kitchen.
items.tip: his = belonging to him (Ben): his breakfast, his bed.

no.he: he goes before a doing word (He eats), not before breakfast.
no.him: him comes after a doing word, but it doesn't say whose breakfast.
no.is: is is a 'be' word; it can't go before breakfast.

items.say: He eats his breakfast in the kitchen.
items.ask: He eats blank breakfast in the kitchen.

items.s: Ben ___ catch a ball in his mouth!
items.tip: can + verb = able to do it: Ben can catch a ball.

no.is: is catch isn't English; is goes with -ing.
no.does: does catch is for questions; to say he is able, we use can.

items.say: Ben can catch a ball in his mouth!
items.ask: Ben blank catch a ball in his mouth!

items.s: He doesn't like cats, ___ he likes rabbits.
items.tip: but shows something different: doesn't like cats, BUT likes rabbits.

no.is: We need a joining word between the two ideas, not is.
no.of: of shows belonging; it can't join two ideas.
no.a: a goes before one thing, not before he.

items.say: He doesn't like cats, but he likes rabbits.
items.ask: He doesn't like cats, blank he likes rabbits.

items.s: At night, Ben sleeps ___ a basket.
items.tip: in = inside something: in a basket, in a box.

no.at: at is for a place we visit (at school), not inside a basket.
no.of: of shows belonging, not a place.
no.an: an goes before a vowel sound, and there's already a.

items.say: At night, Ben sleeps in a basket.
items.ask: At night, Ben sleeps blank a basket.

items.tip: After a doing word we say him, not he: We love him.

no.he: he goes before a doing word (He runs); after love we say him.
no.his: his shows belonging (his bed); it needs a thing after it.
no.they: they is more than one, and after love we'd say them.

items.say: We all love him!
items.ask: We all love blank!
